transcript.content: Hello, how are you today? What brings you in to see me?

Hi, doctor. I'm... doing okay, I suppose. But, well, what brings me in is that I just can't keep my mind on a task long enough to finish it anymore. Even when it's really important. 

Like, I'm a computer support specialist, and I'll start tracing a client's network problem... which, by the way, is getting so much more frustrating lately because everyone is moving to these hybrid cloud setups now. I was just telling my brother—he's also in IT, well, more on the software sales side—that the way these vendors sell these packages, they promise seamless integration, but it's never actually seamless. You always end up with these weird firewall conflicts, and the documentation is always out of date. 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, so I'll be sitting there trying to trace a client's network problem, and ten minutes later I'll realize I've just reread the exact same log entries three times. I just stare at the screen and I still don't know what they say. It's just not sinking in at all.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say I'm feeling down. I mean, I still like doing the things I usually do. Like, I love tinkering with old stereo receivers. I've got this vintage Marantz unit on my workbench right now that I picked up at a garage sale a few weeks ago. The guy selling it had no idea what he had, just thought it was some old junk. It's got this beautiful brushed aluminum faceplate, but the capacitors are totally shot. I was actually looking up replacement parts online last night, and you wouldn't believe how hard it is to find decent audio-grade capacitors these days. A lot of the new stuff is just cheap junk from overseas, and it completely ruins the sound profile. I used to buy from this one supplier in California, but they got bought out by a bigger conglomerate a few years ago, and their quality control just completely tanked. It's a real shame, honestly, because the vintage audio community relies on those parts. But, um... yeah, no, I'm not depressed or anything. I still enjoy my hobbies.
Do you find it hard to focus on things outside of work too, like when you're reading, watching TV, or even talking with someone?

Yeah, it's exactly like what I was saying before about those network logs. It's everywhere. I just can't keep my mind on a task long enough to finish it, even outside of work. 

Like, if I try to watch a movie with my wife... we were trying to watch this new detective show on one of the streaming apps the other night. Which, by the way, we have like four different streaming services now, and it's getting ridiculous. I was looking at our credit card statement the other day, and we're paying more for streaming than we ever did for cable. And the interfaces! As a tech guy, it drives me up the wall. They change the UI every six months just to mess with us, I swear. It takes ten clicks just to find your own watchlist. Back in the day, you just turned on the TV and flipped to channel 4. I actually still have an old CRT TV in the basement, a Sony Trinitron. Best picture tube ever made, but they weigh like a hundred pounds. I had to get my neighbor, Dave, to help me carry it down the stairs last summer. Dave's a good guy, he does landscaping, mostly commercial properties... 

But anyway, sorry, what was I—oh, right. TV and focusing. Yeah, even if we're watching a show I actually really want to see, I'll realize twenty minutes went by and I haven't processed a single word the characters just said. My wife will ask me what I thought of a scene and I draw a complete blank. It's just like the work stuff, my brain just drifts off and none of it sinks in.
Do you often feel restless or as if you need to be doing something constantly, even when you're trying to relax?

Yeah, all the time. It's like... even when I'm supposed to just sit still and relax, or listen to somebody, it feels like there's this motor humming right under my skin. Like I need to stand up, or check my phone, or just move on to the next problem right that second. 

It actually happened just yesterday at the dentist. I was in the chair for a cleaning, and you know how you just have to lie there? Well, my dentist, Dr. Aris, he's great, but he always plays that soft rock station. Which is fine, I guess, but they played this one song by Chicago, and it got me thinking about their brass section. Because, you know, back in the 70s, they had such a distinct sound. My dad used to have all their records on vinyl. He had this massive record collection in the den, and he was so particular about how they were organized. Alphabetical by artist, then chronological by release date. If you put one back in the wrong spot, he'd know instantly. I tried organizing my own digital music library like that once, but the metadata tags on MP3s are always so messed up when you download them. You spend hours fixing the ID3 tags, and then iTunes or whatever just overwrites them anyway. It's infuriating. I ended up writing a Python script to lock the file permissions so the media player couldn't change the tags, which worked for a while, but then... 

Wait, what was I talking about? Oh, right, the restlessness. Yeah, sitting in that dentist chair, listening to Chicago, I just felt this overwhelming urge to get up and do something. Anything. It's just this constant buzzing feeling, you know? Like I can't just be still.
